'''Çetin Kaya Koç''' (born 23 January 1957, [[Ağrı|Ağrı, Turkey]]) is a Turkish-American [[Cryptography|cryptographic engineer]],<ref name=":4">{{cite web | title=Çetin Kaya Koç | date=29 May 2025 | url=https://www.rsaconference.com/experts/etin-kaya-ko }}</ref> academic, and author known for his research and work in cryptographic engineering,<ref name=":0">{{cite web | title=Workshop on Cryptographic Hardware and Embedded Systems (CHES '99) | url=https://iacr.org/workshops/ches/ches99/index.php }}</ref> secure hardware design, [[finite field arithmetic]], and side‑channel security.<ref name=":4" />

He has retired from Computer Science Department at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] and has held permanent academic appointments in the [[United States]], and visiting appointments in Turkey, Italy, and China.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |last=Caroline |date=2013-04-20 |title=Cryptographic Engineering |url=https://mead.ch/mead/cryptographic-engineering/ |access-date=2026-03-25 |website=Mead Education |language=en-US}}</ref>

Koç is the co‑founder of the Conference on Cryptographic Hardware and Embedded Systems (CHES) and the founding ''Editor‑in‑Chief'' of the ''Journal of Cryptographic Engineering''.<ref name=":2">{{cite web | title=Journal of Cryptographic Engineering | url=https://link.springer.com/journal/13389/editorial-board }}</ref>

== Biography & Education ==
Koç was born in [[Ağrı|Ağrı, Turkey]], where he completed his early education before earning a B.S. degree (summa cum laude) in Electrical Engineering from [[İstanbul Technical University]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.yenisafak.com/yazarlar/ersin-celik/boyle-bir-bilim-adami-tayyip-erdogani-nasil-destekler-2060503 |title=Böyle bir bilim adamı Tayyip Erdoğan'ı nasıl destekler? |website=Yeni Şafak |access-date=16 November 2025}}</ref> He then received his Ph.D. in Electrical and Computer Engineering from the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] in 1988, focusing on [[computer architecture]], parallel algorithms and hardware implementations for algebraic computation.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Çetin Kaya Koç {{!}} UCSB Computer Science |url=https://cs.ucsb.edu/people/faculty/cetin-kaya-koc |access-date=2026-02-23 |website=cs.ucsb.edu}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://cetinkayakoc.net/ozgecmis.html |title=Çetin Kaya Koç – Özgeçmiş |website=cetinkayakoc.net |access-date=16 November 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bisav.org.tr/Seminerler/Biyografi/8855/cetin_kaya_koc |title=Çetin Kaya Koç |website=Bilim ve Sanat Vakfı |access-date=16 November 2025}}</ref>

== Career ==
Following his doctoral studies, Koç began his academic career as an assistant professor at the [[University of Houston]] from 1988 to 1992.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://academictree.org/computerscience/peopleinfo.php?pid=191436|title=Computer Science Tree - Çetin Kaya Koç|website=academictree.org}}</ref> He then joined [[Oregon State University]], where he progressed from assistant to full professor (1992–2007) and established the ''Information Security Laboratory'', serving as a central hub for research on secure hardware and embedded [[cryptography]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37326322600|title=Çetin Kaya Koç - IEEE}}</ref>

Koç has held faculty positions at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] and maintained international appointments, including visiting roles at [[Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics]]  and at several universities in Turkey, supervising doctoral and master's candidates and directing collaborative research programs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ORCID |url=https://orcid.org/0000-0002-2572-9565 |access-date=2026-02-23 |website=orcid.org}}</ref>

In 1999, Koç co‑founded the Conference on Cryptographic Hardware and Embedded Systems (CHES) with [[Christof Paar]]. CHES has become one of the premier international fora for research on cryptographic hardware, embedded security, and side‑channel analysis.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sigsac.org/ccs/CCS2020/ashes-proceedings.html|title=Ashes'20 Proceedings}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://easychair.org/cfp/proofs2023|title=CFP|website=easychair.org}}</ref>

Koç has been a foundational figure in cryptographic engineering. He co-founded the Workshop on Cryptographic Hardware and Embedded Systems (CHES) in 1999 and served as program co-chair for five consecutive years (1999–2003) andcontinuously served in the steering committee, establishing CHES as a leading conference in software and hardware realization of cryptography.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cryptocode.com/principal.html|title=Principal|website=cryptocode.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Conference on Cryptographic Hardware and Embedded Systems (CHES) |url=https://dblp.uni-trier.de/db/conf/ches/index.html |access-date=2026-02-25 |website=dblp.uni-trier.de |language=en}}</ref>

He also founded and served as Editor-in-Chief of the ''Journal of Cryptographic Engineering'', overseeing its inaugural publication and shaping it into a premier venue for research on cryptographic hardware and embedded systems.<ref name=":2" /> Koç contributed to practical cryptographic software development, notably as one of the designers of the RSAREF software toolkit, a widely used [[reference implementation]] of RSA cryptography.<ref>{{cite book | last1=Acıiçmez | first1=Onur | last2=Koç | first2=Çetin Kaya | last3=Seifert | first3=Jean-Pierre | title=Topics in Cryptology – CT-RSA 2007 | chapter=Predicting Secret Keys Via Branch Prediction | series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science | date=2006 | volume=4377 | pages=225–242 | doi=10.1007/11967668_15 | isbn=978-3-540-69327-7 | chapter-url=https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1007/11967668_15 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Prima |date=2007-09-06 |title=Une faille de sécurité dans les processeurs |url=https://interstices.info/une-faille-de-securite-dans-les-processeurs/ |access-date=2026-02-25 |website=Interstices |language=fr-FR|first=Jean - Michel}}</ref>

== Research and works ==
His work has been recognized with prestigious awards, including the ACM CCS Test of Time Award <ref>{{Cite web |title=Test-of-Time Awards - ACM ASIACCS 2025 - HUST |url=https://asiaccs2025.hust.edu.vn/test-of-time-award-2/ |website=AsiaCCS |date=12 January 2025 }}</ref> and the USENIX 2024 Distinguished Paper Award.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-04-30 |title=USENIX Security '24 Fall Accepted Papers |url=https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity24/fall-accepted-papers |access-date=2026-02-23 |website=USENIX |language=en}}</ref> An accomplished author, he has published books such as ''Cryptographic Engineering'' (2009),<ref name=":3" /> ''Cryptographic Algorithms on Reconfigurable Hardware'',<ref name=":7">{{Cite book |title=Cryptographic Algorithms on Reconfigurable Hardware |date=2006 |publisher=Springer Science+Business Media, LLC |isbn=978-0-387-33883-5 |editor-last=Rodríguez-Henríquez |editor-first=Francisco |series=Signals and Communication Technology |location=Boston, MA |editor-last2=Pérez |editor-first2=Arturo Díaz |editor-last3=Saqib |editor-first3=Nazar Abbas |editor-last4=Koç |editor-first4=Çetin Kaya|url=https://www.aiu.edu.sy/es/1-13531/book/10347/978-0-387-36682-1/Cryptographic-Algorithms-on-Reconfigurable-Hardware}}</ref> ''Partially Homomorphic Encryption'',<ref>{{Cite book |last=Koç |first=Çetin Kaya |title=Partially Homomorphic Encryption |date=2021 |publisher=Springer International Publishing AG |others=Funda Özdemir, Zeynep Ödemiş Özger |isbn=978-3-030-87628-9 |location=Cham}}</ref> and several monographs on finite field arithmetic and post-quantum cryptography.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Savas |first1=Erkay |last2=Koc |first2=Cetin |date=2010 |title=Finite Field Arithmetic for Cryptography |journal=IEEE Circuits and Systems Magazine |volume=10 |issue=2 |pages=40–56 |doi=10.1109/MCAS.2010.936785 |issn=1531-636X}}</ref>

Koç is the first researcher who coined or invented the term "Cryptographic Engineering" and started using it actively: as the name of a course offered at EPFL, Switzerland every year since 2002,<ref name=":6" /> the name of a book,<ref name=":3" /> and the name of the journal he had founded.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Journal of Cryptographic Engineering |url=https://link.springer.com/journal/13389 |access-date=2026-03-25 |website=SpringerLink |language=en}}</ref> Koç described the detailed definition and history of cryptographic engineering in an article published in 2011, entitled "Introduction to Cryptographic Engineering".<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Koç |first=Çetin Kaya |date=2011-04-01 |title=Introduction to the Journal of Cryptographic Engineering |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s13389-011-0007-x |journal=Journal of Cryptographic Engineering |language=en |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=1–3 |doi=10.1007/s13389-011-0007-x |issn=2190-8516}}</ref>

Koç’s research contributions span multiple foundational areas in cryptographic engineering and secure computation.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":3">{{cite book | editor-first1=Çetin Kaya | editor-last1=Koç | title=Cryptographic Engineering | date=2009 | doi=10.1007/978-0-387-71817-0 | isbn=978-0-387-71816-3 | url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-0-387-71817-0 }}</ref><ref>https://www.cryptocode.com/</ref> His work in ''cryptographic engineering'' focuses on the design and optimization of secure hardware and software implementations of cryptographic systems, including practical realizations of public‑key and [[Symmetric-key algorithm|symmetric algorithms]], secure embedded systems, and high‑performance cryptographic components for real‑world applications.<ref name=":7" /><ref name=":5" />

He has played a leading role in developing architectures and algorithms for finite field and ring arithmetic, which underpin efficient modular multiplication and exponentiation used in public‑key protocols, elliptic‑curve [[cryptography]], and error‑correcting codes.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Yao |first1=Gavin Xiaoxu |last2=Cheung |first2=Ray C.C. |last3=Koç |first3=Ç Kaya |last4=Man |first4=Kim Fung |chapter=Reconfigurable Number Theoretic Transform architectures for cryptographic applications |date=2010 |title=2010 International Conference on Field-Programmable Technology |pages=308–311 |doi=10.1109/FPT.2010.5681440|isbn=978-1-4244-8980-0 }}</ref><ref name=":0" />

His work addresses challenges in random number generation, privacy‑preserving computation,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hu |first1=Sen |last2=Ci |first2=Shang |last3=Guan |first3=Donghai |last4=Koç |first4=Çetin Kaya |date=2025 |title=SOCT: Secure Outsourcing Computation Toolkit Using Threshold ElGamal Algorithm |journal=IEEE Transactions on Cloud Computing |volume=13 |issue=2 |pages=711–720 |doi=10.1109/TCC.2025.3561313 |bibcode=2025ITCC...13..711H |issn=2168-7161}}</ref> and the application of ''homomorphic encryption to'' ''machine learning''.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Koç |first=Çetin Kaya |chapter=Formidable Challenges in Hardware Implementations of Fully Homomorphic Encryption Functions for Applications in Machine Learning |date=2020 |title=Proceedings of the 4th ACM Workshop on Attacks and Solutions in Hardware Security |chapter-url=https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3411504.3421208 |language=en |publisher=ACM |pages=3 |doi=10.1145/3411504.3421208 |isbn=978-1-4503-8090-4|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In more recent work, he has contributed to [[Post-quantum cryptography|post‑quantum cryptography]] and [[homomorphic encryption]], co‑authoring monographs on partially homomorphic schemes and exploring secure computation models that allow operations on encrypted data without decryption.<ref>{{Citation |last1=Barreto |first1=Paulo S. L. Salina |last7=Pereira |first7=Geovandro C. C. == Awards and honours ==
Koç has been recognized by both academic institutions and professional societies for his contributions to cryptographic engineering and secure system design.

* 2001 – Award for Outstanding and Sustained Research Leadership, Oregon State University.<ref>{{Cite web|author1=Anonymous |url=https://engineering.oregonstate.edu/awards|title=College of Engineering Awards – Oregon State University|work=College of Engineering |date=20 September 2014 |access-date=13 November 2025}}</ref>
* 2007 – Elected Fellow of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) for contributions to cryptographic engineering.<ref name=":8" />
* 2020 – International Fellowship for Outstanding Researchers, Scientific and Technological Research Council of Türkiye (TÜBİTAK).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tubitak.gov.tr/en/announcements/international-fellowship-program|title=TÜBİTAK International Fellowship Program|publisher=TÜBİTAK|access-date=13 November 2025}}</ref>
* 2023 – Life Fellow of the IEEE for sustained contributions to cryptographic engineering.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cetinkayakoc.net/|title=Çetin Kaya Koç – Official Website|website=cetinkayakoc.net|access-date=13 November 2025}}</ref><ref name=":8">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ieee.org/membership/fellows/index.html|title=IEEE Fellows Directory|publisher=IEEE|access-date=13 November 2025}}</ref>
